==English== {{swp|}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|sĕt}}, {{IPA|en|/sɛt/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-set.ogg|a=US}} * {{homophones|en|sett}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛt|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== {{ety|en|id=put down|:inh|enm:setten|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|setten|}}, from {{inh|en|ang|settan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sattjan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*satjaną}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*sodéyeti}}, causative of {{m|ine-pro|*sed-||to sit}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|zetten}}, {{cog|de|setzen}}, {{cog|da|sætte}}, {{cog|nb|sette}}, {{cog|is,nn|setja}}, {{cog|sv|sätta}}, {{cog|fo|seta}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb|~s|~ting|~|+,~ten}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[put]] (something) down, to [[rest]]. #: {{syn|en|put|lay|set down}} #: {{ant|en|pick up}} #: {{ux|en|'''Set''' the [[tray]] there.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To attach or affix (something) to something else, or in or upon a certain place. #: {{ux|en|I have '''set''' my heart on running the marathon.}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Genesis|4|15|passage=The Lord '''set''' a mark upon Cain.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To put in a specified condition or state; to cause to be. #* {{RQ:KJV|Deuteronomy|28|1|passage=The Lord thy God will '''set''' thee on high.}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Matthew|10|35|passage=I am come to '''set''' a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1827|author=w:Samuel Taylor Coleridge|title=Hamlet |passage=Every incident '''sets''' him thinking.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[start]] (a [[fire]]). #: {{syn|en|light}} #: {{ant|en|extinguish|put out|quench}} # {{lb|en|transitive|dated}} To cause to stop or stick; to obstruct; to fasten to a spot. #: {{ux|en|to '''set''' a coach in the mud}} # {{senseid|en|determine}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To [[determine]] or [[settle]]. #: {{ux|en|to '''set''' the rent}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[adjust]]. #: {{ux|en|I '''set''' the alarm at 6 a.m.}} (i.e. I programmed it at that hour to go off at a later time) #: {{ux|en|I '''set''' the alarm for 6 a.m.}} (i.e. I programmed it earlier to go off at that hour.) # {{lb|en|transitive}} To punch (a [[nail]]) into [[wood]] so that its head is below the surface. # {{lb|en|transitive}} To arrange with [[dish]]es and [[cutlery]], to [[set the table]]. #: {{ux|en|Please '''set''' the table for our guests.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[introduce]] or [[describe]]. #: {{ux|en|I’ll tell you what happened, but first let me '''set''' the scene.}} #* {{RQ:Fielding Tom Jones|chapter=II|passage=An incident which happened about this time will '''set''' the characters of these two lads more fairly before the discerning reader than is in the power of the longest dissertation.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[locate]] (a play, etc.); to assign a [[backdrop]] to, geographically or temporally. #: {{ux|en|He says he will '''set''' his next film in France.}} #: {{ux|en|Her debut novel is '''set''' during the U.S. Civil War.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[compile]], to make (a puzzle or challenge). #: {{ux|en|This crossword was '''set''' by Araucaria.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To prepare (a stage or film set). # {{lb|en|transitive}} To fit (someone) up in a situation. # {{lb|en|transitive}} To arrange (type). #: {{syn|en|typeset}} #: {{ux|en|It was a complex page, but he '''set''' it quickly.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[devise]] and [[assign]] (work) to. #: {{ux|en|The teacher '''set''' her students the task of drawing a foot.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|volleyball}} To direct (the ball) to a teammate for an attack. # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[gel#Verb|gel]]; to [[solidify]]. #: {{syn|en|set up#Verb|cure#Verb|jell#Verb|jell out#Etymology_2}} #: {{ux|en|This [[glue#Noun|glue]] '''sets''' in five minutes.}} #: {{ux|en|This [[jelly#Noun|jelly]] '''sets''' within a few hours when refrigerated.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To render stiff or solid; especially, to convert into curd; to curdle. #: {{ux|en|to '''set''' milk for cheese}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} Of a heavenly body, to disappear below the [[horizon]] of a planet, etc, as the latter rotates. #: {{ux|en|The moon '''sets''' at eight o'clock tonight.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|bridge}} To [[defeat]] a [[contract]]. # {{lb|en|obsolete|now followed by "out", as in [[set out]]}} To begin to move; to [[go forth]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 5|text=The king is '''set''' from London, and the scene is now transported, gentles, to Southampton}} # {{lb|en|transitive|botany}} To produce after pollination. #: {{ux|en|to '''set''' seed}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Daniel Chamovitz|title=What a Plant Knows|page=155 |passage=Many fruit trees will only flower and '''set''' fruit following a cold winter.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|of fruit}} To be fixed for growth; to strike root; to begin to germinate or form. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1906|author=Canada. Dept. of Agriculture. Fruit Branch|title=Fruit crop report |passage=In the Annapolis Valley, in spite of an irregular bloom, the fruit has '''set''' well and has, as yet, been little affected by scab.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|Southern US|Midwestern US|dialects}} To [[sit]] {{gloss|be in a seated position}}. #: {{ux|en|He '''sets''' in that chair all day.}} #* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=7|passage=Old Applegate, in the stern, just '''set''' and looked at me, and Lord James, amidship, waved both arms and kept hollering for help. I took a couple of everlasting big strokes and managed to grab hold of the skiff's rail, close to the stern.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1987|author=Toni Morrison|title=Beloved|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=sfmp6gjZGP8C&pg=PA227|page=227 |passage=And if Mrs. Garner didn't need me right there in the kitchen, I could get a chair and you and me could '''set''' out there while I did the vegetables.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|Southern US|Midwestern US|dialects}} To [[rest]] or [[lie]] somewhere, on something, etc.; to occupy a certain place. #* {{quote-song|en|year=1975|lyricist=C.W. McCall; Chip Davis|title={{w|Convoy (song)|Convoy}}|album=Black Bear Road|url=|artist=w:C. W. McCall|passage=Well, we rolled up Interstate 44
Like a rocket-sled on rails.
We tore up all of our swindle sheets
And left 'em '''settin'''' on the scales.}} # To hunt game with the aid of a [[setter]]. # {{senseid|en|hunting}}{{lb|en|hunting|ambitransitive}} Of a dog, to indicate the position of [[game]]. #: {{ux|en|The dog '''sets''' the bird.}} #: {{ux|en|Your dog '''sets''' well.}} # To apply oneself; to undertake earnestly. #* {{RQ:Hammond Of Fundamentals |passage=If he '''set''' industriously and sincerely to perform the commands of Christ, he can have no ground of doubting but it shall prove successful to him.}} # {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To fit music to words. #* {{RQ:Dryden Mac Flecknoe|passage='''Set''' thy own songs, and sing them to thy lute.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Two Gentlemen of Verona|1|2|passage=That I might sing it (Madam) to a tune:
Giue me a Note, your Ladiship can '''set'''}} # {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To place plants or shoots in the ground; to plant. #: {{ux|en|to '''set''' pear trees in an orchard}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1774|author=John Robinson; Thomas Rispin|title=A Journey Through Nova-Scotia|location=York|publisher=C. Etherington|pageurl=https://hdl.handle.net/2027/aeu.ark:/13960/t56d6f521?urlappend=%3Bseq=24|page=19 |passage=We saw him with eight men '''setting''' potatoes within a week of mid-summer.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1915|author={{w|D. H. Lawrence}}|journal=The Rainbow|publisher=Vintage|year_published=2011|page=204 |passage=At Eastertime one year, she helped him to '''set''' potatoes.}} # To become [[fixed]] or [[rigid]]; to be [[fastened]]. # To have a certain direction of motion; to flow; to move on; to tend. #: {{ux|en|The current '''sets''' to the north; the tide '''sets''' to the windward.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|country dancing}} To acknowledge a dancing partner by facing them and moving first to one side and then to the other, while they do the opposite. #: {{ux|en|'''Set''' to partners! was the next instruction from the caller.}} # To place or fix in a [[setting]]. #: {{ux|en|to '''set''' a precious stone in a border of metal}} #: {{ux|en|to '''set''' glass in a sash}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Spanish Fryar|58|And him too rich a jewel to be '''set''' / In vulgar metal for a vulgar use.}} # To put in order in a particular manner; to prepare. #: {{ux|en|to '''set''' (that is, to hone) a razor}} #: {{ux|en|to '''set''' a saw}} # To extend and bring into position; to spread. #: {{ux|en|to '''set''' the sails of a ship}} # To give a pitch to, as a tune; to start by fixing the keynote. #* {{RQ:Fielding Joseph Andrews|volume=I|chapter=Here Joseph Andrews Writ a Letter to His Sister Pamela|page=25|passage={{...}} I ſhould be very vvilling to be his Clerk; for vvhich you knovv I am qualified, being able to read, and to '''ſet''' a Pſalm.}} # To reduce from a [[dislocated]] or [[fractured]] state. #: {{ux|en|to '''set''' a broken bone}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|now|dialectal}} To [[sit]] or [[lie]] (easily etc.) on the [[stomach]]; to be [[digested]] in a certain manner. # {{lb|en|masonry}} To lower into place and fix solidly, as the blocks of cut stone in a structure. # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To wager in gambling; to risk. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Richard 3|V|iv|passage=I have '''set''' my life upon a cast, / And I will stand the hazard of the die.}} # To adorn with something infixed or affixed; to stud; to variegate with objects placed here and there. #* {{RQ:Dryden Fables|The Flower and the Leaf |passage=High on their heads, with jewels richly '''set''', / Each lady wore a radiant coronet.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1815|author=w:William Wordsworth|title=Poems of the Imagination |passage=pastoral dales thin '''set''' with modern farms}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To value; to rate; used with ''at''. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 4-2|V|ii|passage=Be you contented, wearing now the garland, / To have a son '''set''' your decrees at naught.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Hamlet|I|iv|passage=I do not '''set''' my life at a pin's fee.}} # To establish as a rule; to furnish; to prescribe; to assign. #: {{ux|en|to '''set''' a good example}} # {{lb|en|Scotland}} To suit; to become. #: {{ux|en|It '''sets''' him ill.}} # To cause (a domestic fowl) to sit on eggs to brood. #: {{uxi|en|To '''set''' a hen.}} # To arrange the casting of a movie. #: {{ux|en|Paramount Pictures has '''set''' Jennifer Love Hewitt for a movie called ''Two Can Play This Game''.}} =====Usage notes===== * Originally, ''set'' specifically served as the causative of ''sit'', and this relationship is still reflected in several of the above senses. However, as with many such pairs, the correspondence has mostly deteriorated, with new senses of ''sit'' no longer being accompanied with a like sense of ''set''; notably, there are now transitive senses of ''sit'' and intransitive senses of ''set''. Compare {{m|en|rise}} and {{m|en|raise}}, whose senses are almost all intransitive and transitive counterparts, respectively. =====Conjugation===== subpage|Etymology 1}} ===Etymology 2=== {{ety|en|id=punch|:inh|enm:set}} From {{inh|en|enm|set}}, {{m|enm|sette}}, from {{inh|en|ang|set|t=seat, place of residence, camp, settlement, entrenchment, pattern of behaviour. # {{lb|en|piledriving}} A piece placed temporarily upon the head of a [[pile]] when the latter cannot otherwise be reached by the weight, or hammer. # {{lb|en|printing|dated}} The [[width]] of the [[body]] of a [[type]]. # A [[young]] [[oyster]] when first [[attach]]ed. # Collectively, the [[crop]] of young oysters in any [[locality]]. # {{senseid|en|series or group}} A series or group of something. (''Note the similar meaning in {{l|en|set|Etymology 4, Noun|id=matching collection}}'') # {{lb|en|colloquial}} The [[manner]], [[state]], or [[quality]] of setting or [[fit]]ting; [[fit]]. #: {{ux|en|the '''set''' of a coat}} #* {{RQ:Bramah Bravo of London|passage=Mr. Joolby lay on the floor beside his special chair, his face doubly terrible in its rigid '''set''', his body writhing this way and that with spasmodic jerks and contortions.}} # The [[pattern]] of a [[tartan]], etc. # The [[camber]] of a curved roofing tile. # The full number of [[egg]]s set under a [[hen]]. # {{lb|en|obsolete|rare}} That which is [[stake]]d; a [[wager]]; hence, a gambling game. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 5|I|ii|passage=We will in France, by God's grace, play a '''set''' / Shall strike his father's crown into the hazard.}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Hind and Panther |passage=That was but civil war, an equal '''set'''.}} #* {{RQ:Dickens Little Dorrit|passage=Thenceforth the Dowager, with a light and careless humour, often recounted to her particular acquaintance how, after a hard trial, she had found it impossible to know those people who belonged to Henry’s wife, and who had made that desperate '''set''' to catch him.}} # A [[tool]] for [[dress]]ing [[forge]]d [[iron]]. =====Derived terms===== {{col4|en|title=Terms derived from ''set'' (noun) |compression set|set dec|rearset|setless|setmaker |dead set|set dresser|butt set|time-point set |level set|marzipan set|set light|stop set|instruction set architecture |offset|hookset |onset |outset |seam set |set-off |set tool |set-top box|rivet set|radio set |television set |TV set}} =====Translations===== {{see translation subpage|Etymology 2}} ===Etymology 3=== {{ety|en|id=fixed in position|:inh|enm:sett}} From {{inh|en|enm|sett}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ġesett}}, past participle of {{m|ang|settan}}. ====Adjective==== {{wikidata lexeme|L340344}} {{en-adj}} # [[fixed|Fixed]] in position. # [[rigid|Rigid]], solidified. # [[ready|Ready]], [[prepared]]. #: {{ux|en|[[on your mark, get set, go|on your marks, get '''set''', go!]];  [[on your marks]], '''set''', go!}} # [[intent|Intent]], [[determine]]d (to do something). #: {{ux|en|'''set''' on getting to his destination}} #* {{RQ:Stevenson Osbourne Wrecker|chapter=In which Jim and I Take Different Ways|page=179|passage=And she likes you so much, and thinks you so accomplished and distingué-looking, and was just as '''set''' as I was to have you for best man.}} # [[prearrange|Prearranged]]. #: {{uxi|en|a [[set menu]]|t=a meal that is instituted by a [[restaurateur]] for a limited occasion}} #: {{uxi|en|a '''set''' book|t=a required reading for a course in an educational institution}} # {{U|fixed}} in one’s [[opinion]]. #: {{ux|en|I’m '''set''' against the idea of smacking children to punish them.}} # {{lb|en|of hair}} Fixed in a certain style. =====Synonyms===== * {{sense|intent, determined}} {{l|en|determined}}, {{l|en|intent}} * {{sense|prearranged}} {{l|en|dictated}}, {{l|en|prearranged}}, {{l|en|predetermined}}, {{l|en|prescribed}}, {{l|en|specified}} * {{sense|fixed in one's opinion}} {{l|en|fixed}}, {{l|en|rigid}} =====Derived terms===== {{col3|en|title=Terms derived from Etymology 3 |all set|set point theory|misset |close-set|aforeset |dead set |dead set against |deep-set |hard-set |have one's heart set on |heavyset,heavy-set |nail set|set book |mindset |offset |outset |photoset |preset |quickset |set-aside |saw set |self-set |set back |setback |set chisel |set fair |set for life |sethood |set-in |set in one's ways |setlist |setness |set net |set of one's jaw |set phrase |set shot |set square |set-stitched |setter |set-to |sharp-set |thickset |trendsetter |typeset |unset |upset |well-set|set screw|go set }} =====Translations===== {{see translation subpage|Etymology 3}} ===Etymology 4=== {{ety|en|id=young plant|:inh|enm:set}} From {{der|en|enm|set}}, {{m|enm|sete}}, {{m|enm|sette||that which is set, the act of setting, seat}}, from {{der|en|ang|set||setting, seat, a place where people remain, habitation, camp, entrenchment, a place where animals are kept, stall, fold}} and {{der|en|ang|seten||a set, shoot, slip, branch; a nursery, plantation; that which is planted or set; a cultivated place; planting, cultivation; a setting, putting; a stopping; occupied land}}, related to {{cog|ang|settan||to set}}. Compare {{cog|gml|gesette||a set, suite}}, {{cog|ang|gesetl||assembly}}. According to Skeat, in senses denoting a group of things or persons, representing an alteration of {{m|en|sept}}, from {{der|en|fro|sette||a religious sect}}, from {{der|en|la-med|secta||retinue}}, from {{der|en|la|secta||a faction}}. See {{l|en|sect}}. It is quite possible that the modern word is more of a merger between both, however. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # A young plant fit for setting out; a [[slip]]; [[shoot]]. # A rudimentary fruit. # The setting of the sun or other luminary; {{lb|en|by extension}} the close of the day. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Richard 3|act=V|scene=iii|passage=The weary sun hath made a golden '''set'''.}} #* {{RQ:Tennyson Poems 1842|volume=I|poem=Adeline|page=41|passage=And a rose-bush leans upon, / Thou that faintly smilest still, / As a Naiad in a well, / Looking at the '''set''' of day, {{...}}}} # {{lb|en|literally|and|figuratively}} General [[movement]]; [[direction]]; [[drift]]; [[tendency]]. #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1840|author=w:Thomas De Quincey|journal=Style |passage=Here and there, amongst individuals alive to the particular evils of the age, and watching the very '''set''' of the current, there may have been even a more systematic counteraction applied to the mischief.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1951|author=Herman Wouk|title=The Caine Mutiny|page=238|passage=He put his eye to the alidade. “I thought so! Zero ''five'' four and that's allowing nothing for '''set''' and drift along the line of bearing. We're inside the departure point now{{...}}”}} # {{senseid|en|matching collection}} A [[match]]ing [[collection]] of similar things. (''Note the similar meaning in {{l|en|set|Etymology 2, Noun|id=series or group}}''.) #: {{ux|en|a '''set''' of tables}} # A collection of various objects for a particular purpose. #: {{ux|en|a '''set''' of tools}} # An object made up of several parts. #: {{ux|en|a '''set''' of steps}} # {{senseid|en|math-collection}}{{lb|en|set theory}} A collection of zero or more [[object]]s, possibly infinite in size, and disregarding any order or repetition of the objects which may be contained within it. # {{lb|en|in plural, "sets"|mathematics|informal}} [[set theory|Set theory]]. # A group of people, usually meeting socially or connected through some shared interest, activity, attribute, etc. #: {{ux|en|the country '''set'''}} #* {{RQ:Thackeray Pendennis|chapter=XIX|passage=That he took perfumed baths is a truth; and he used to say that he took them after meeting certain men of a very low '''set''' in hall.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1889|year_published=1899|author={{w|Rudyard Kipling}}|title={{w|Under the Deodars}}|chapter=The Education of Otis Yeere|location= Boston|publisher=The Greenock Press|page=21|text=“Good gracious, child, you didn't join the Theosophists and kiss Buddha's big toe, did you ? I tried to get into their '''set''' once, but they cast me out for a sceptic — without a chance of improving my poor little mind, too.”}} # The [[scenery]] for a [[film]] or [[play]]. # The general [[locations]] and [[area]] where a [[movie]]’s, a [[film]]’s, or a [[video]]’s [[scenery]] is arranged to be filmed also including places for [[actors]], assorted crew, [[director]], [[producer]]s which are typically not filmed. # {{lb|en|dance}} The initial or basic [[formation]] of [[dancer]]s. # {{senseid|en|exercise}} {{lb|en|exercise}} A group of [[repetition]]s of a single [[exercise]] performed one after the other without rest. #: {{mer|en|rep}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1974|author=Charles Gaines; George Butler|title=Pumping Iron: The Art and Sport of Bodybuilding|page=22 |passage=This is the fourth '''set''' of benchpresses.}} # {{senseid|en|tennis}} {{lb|en|tennis}} A complete series of [[game]]s, forming part of a [[match]]. # {{lb|en|volleyball}} A complete series of [[point]]s, forming part of a [[match]]. # {{lb|en|volleyball}} The act of directing the ball to a teammate for an [[attack]]. # {{senseid|en|musical performance comprising several pieces}} {{lb|en|music}} A musical [[performance]] by a [[band]], [[disc jockey]], etc., consisting of several musical pieces. #* {{RQ:Guardian|date=June 26, 2017|author=Alexis Petridis| title=Glastonbury 2017 verdict: Radiohead, Foo Fighters, Lorde, Stormzy and more| url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2017/jun/26/glastonbury-2017-verdict-radiohead-foo-fighters-lorde-stormzy-and-more| passage=You heard “oh, Jeremy Corbyn” everywhere: at the silent disco, during Radiohead’s Friday night headlining '''set''', midway through the Other stage appearance by rapper Stormzy, who gamely joined in. |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261012112015/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2017/jun/26/glastonbury-2017-verdict-radiohead-foo-fighters-lorde-stormzy-and-more|archivedate=12 October 2026}} # {{lb|en|music}} A [[drum kit]], a [[drum set]]. #: {{ux|en|He plays the '''set''' on Saturdays.}} # {{lb|en|UK|education}} A class group in a subject where pupils are divided by ability. # {{lb|en|poker|slang}} [[three of a kind|Three of a kind]], especially if two cards are in one's [[hand]] and the third is on the [[board]].
